ideas.title: The friends pull my first cart up the dune, then the motor drags them back down
ideas.goal: Before it has a motor, the friends pull Lumi's wooden cart up the dune on a rope, feet slipping in the sand; the player picks wheel width and who pulls; then the motor goes on the axle and the same friends try to hold the cart back in a tug of war they lose, sliding down the dune after it. Fun because the friends play with the machine, the player's wheel choice decides whether it climbs, and the motor's worth shows in friends.
ideas.toward: Road steps 'wheels and frame with rolling contact on the terrain' and 'the cart drives because the parts do': frame and wheels before the motor, then the Drum motor (s157: starts from every angle) on them.
ideas.idea: The cart as PrintSim rigid bodies (frame, axle, wheels on revolute joints). Wheel-sand contact by Bekker pressure-sinkage: a 15 kg cart with two friends aboard puts ~90 N on each 3 cm rim, which sinks ~1 cm in loose dry sand (kc ~ 1 kN/m^(n+1), kphi ~ 1500 kN/m^(n+2), n ~ 1.1): visible ruts written into the terrain, and the rolling resistance from that sinkage is what makes narrow rims bog and wide ones climb. The friends are not posed by a clip: the rope's tension acts on each puller's body as a force; it holds while the tension is under its weight times the sand's friction at its feet, and past that its feet slide in the sand (the same rule for any creature on any ground); it leans by the rope's angle so its centre of mass stays over its feet. Then the motor's torque through the wheels against the friends' traction decides the tug of war. Watching: three friends dig in and inch the cart up, ruts behind it; at the top Lumi touches the last wire, the cart pulls away, Truffle hangs on and slides down the dune behind it on its belly.
ideas.form: Plugin on the dune: cart, rope, terrain ruts, friend behaviour 'pull' driven by the rope's force, then the Drum motor fitted; a traced film low beside the cart.

ideas.title: A lift up the cairn that brakes itself on the way down
ideas.goal: A platform on a rope from the motor's spool at the top of the cairn; friends walk onto it at the bottom by themselves and the motor hauls them up to the lookout; too many and it stalls, then sinks back slowly, because a motor turned backwards brakes itself. The player adds cells, a bigger spool or a counterweight stone until the whole family gets up. Fun because the friends want to ride, the load is them, and the slow sink is a gentle failure.
ideas.toward: Road steps 'the generator' and 'braking that charges the cells': a motor driven backwards makes current and resists, from the same circuit; the first machine the friends ride.
ideas.idea: No stepping into a basket: a flat wooden platform that rests on the ground, so the friends simply walk onto it with their normal walk. The platform is a rigid body; its load is the sum of the contact forces under whatever stands on it (a friend, a stone, a crate: any mass counts the same, nothing tells it who is aboard), carried by an XPBD rope to the spool. The spool's torque comes from the Drum solve; when the load wins, the rotor turns backwards, its back-EMF drives a current through the coils and cells that opposes the motion (dynamic braking, no brake code), and the descent speed comes out of the winding's resistance (short the cells and it sinks slower still). A friend whose mood wants a view walks to the platform and waits; at the top it walks off to look out. Watching: Gloop and Truffle ride up, Pickles walks on too, it stops, sinks gently while the motor hums backwards, Pickles walks off grumbling, up it goes.
ideas.form: Plugin at the cairn: platform, rope, the Drum motor in real copper, iron and wood, friend behaviour 'ride up'.
